flashcards.demoDescription: This demo shows how Flashcards can turn your content into spaced‑repetition cards. Connect your own server later to generate and review cards from your own notes and media.
flashcards.demoExample1: See how decks, cards, and tags are organized across Review and Manage tabs.
flashcards.demoExample2: When you connect, you’ll be able to generate cards from lectures, meetings, or notes and review them on a schedule.
flashcards.demoExample3: Use Flashcards together with Notes and Media to keep important ideas fresh.
flashcards.demoSample1Summary: 10 cards · Great for testing spacing and ratings.
flashcards.demoSample2Summary: 8 cards · Names, acronyms, and key definitions.
flashcards.demoSample3Summary: 6 cards · Example action items to review.
flashcards.demoCard1Back: A learning technique that reviews material at increasing intervals based on how well you remember it. Cards you know well are shown less often; cards you struggle with are shown more frequently.
flashcards.demoCard2Front: What does RAG stand for in AI?
flashcards.demoCard2Back: Retrieval-Augmented Generation — a technique that enhances LLM responses by retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base before generating an answer.
flashcards.demoCard3Front: What is the difference between a podcast and an audiobook?
flashcards.demoCard3Back: Podcasts are episodic audio series, often conversational, released on a schedule. Audiobooks are narrated versions of written books, typically consumed as a complete work.
flashcards.demoCard4Back: A unique identifier used to authenticate requests to an API. Like a password for software — it proves your application is authorized to access the service.
flashcards.demoCard5Back: A learning method: (1) Choose a concept, (2) Explain it simply as if teaching a child, (3) Identify gaps in your explanation, (4) Review and simplify further.
flashcards.demoPreviewDescription: This is a preview. Connect a server to create your own decks with spaced repetition.
